about: Known answers for routing and shape prediction. Read by dobladillo.benchmark; run with `dobladillo benchmark`. Design paths are relative to this file. Every entry cites where its answer comes from; none comes from a tool this project wrote.

composite-beam theory (any strength-of-materials text, e.g. Timoshenko & Gere): six helices on a hexagon of circumradius D, one wanting to be 1/21 shorter, kappa = S eps D / (3 S D^2 + 6 EI), R = 168.0 nm with the model's own S, EI and D, toward the short helix. Twist-stretch coupling off, because the formula has none. Graded by mechanics.twin: radius within 1%, direction within 1 deg
composite-beam theory: half the misfit strain, twice the radius (336 nm)
symmetry: opposite helices shortened equally leave no moment about the centroid, so the bundle shortens and stays straight (to within 1% of one helix's curvature; see mechanics.twin.STRAIGHT_REL_TOL)

cases.conditions: negative-stain TEM, particles with three clear stripes only; buffer not transcribed
cases.source: Dietz, Douglas & Shih, Science 325, 725 (2009), Fig. 3K, NIH author manuscript PMC2737683: 121 deg +- 8.4 deg s.d., N = 212, for the design programmed to bend 120 deg
cases.known_failure: The beam model with default parameters predicts 101 deg, 2.3 s.d. below the measured mean. With twist-stretch coupling switched off it predicts 118 deg, inside. Whether the coupling term is wrong in this model or the measurement differs (dried, stained particles) is not settled. The 2 s.d. band is a convention, and it was fixed AFTER both numbers had been computed, so this is not a blind criterion

wanted.why_not: the measured angles are in the open author manuscript (PMC2737683), but the design files are not in any openly licensed source checked: caDNAno 2.5's test data holds only the 120 deg design and the beach ball. The paper's supplementary materials (science.org) were not examined for design files, and no open licence for them was found. Rebuilding the designs from the paper's description would make them ours, not the published ones
